subject: Attribution addendum request — network tail exclusion for private VPC
messages:
From: Samira Patel <samira@oriontech.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: Amit Rao <amit@oriontech.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700 (PDT)
Subject: Request: carveout for customer-controlled network segments (private VPC)

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday — the Redwood demo helped a lot. Before we proceed to procurement, our security and infra teams have one request that will need to be reflected in our SOW/SLA: for private VPC deployments where OrionTech controls the VPC peering, on-prem networking, and transit providers, we need explicit language that excludes outages or latency attributable to customer-controlled network segments from Redwood uptime/latency calculations and credits.

We drafted a short explanation and a suggested paragraph (attached) to use as an addendum. High-level asks:
- Exclude customer-managed network transit, peering misconfigurations, and vendor transit provider incidents from Redwood availability calculations for Private deployments.
- Define the evidence required (traces, BGP logs, timestamps) to establish attribution.
- Keep Redwood SLA for compute/hosted runtime components intact.

Can your team review and let us know if Redwood is comfortable with a narrowly scoped addendum and the evidence list? If yes we'll loop in procurement/legal to get the paperwork moving.

Attachment: network-topology.pdf (diagram of OrionTech private VPC peering and transit providers)

Best,
Samira
Samira Patel
Senior Cloud Security Engineer, OrionTech
samira@oriontech.com
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Patel <samira@oriontech.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 17:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: carveout for customer-controlled network segments (private VPC)

Hi Samira — thanks for the clear summary and the diagram.

We can absolutely consider a narrowly scoped addendum for Private deployments that attributes incidents to customer-managed network components when the evidence meets an agreed threshold. I'll coordinate with Vivek and Irene on security/legal language and get a draft back to you by end of day tomorrow.

Couple of quick clarifying questions that will help the draft:
- Do you expect attribution to rely on packet captures, BGP update logs, or both? (short answer is fine)
- Are there particular transit providers you want explicitly called out?

We'll propose specific evidence requirements and a short escalation timeline in the draft.

Thanks — Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 18:00:00 +0000
Subject: INTERNAL: OrionTech carveout — evidence bar and risk notes

Vivek/Irene — looping you in on OrionTech's request. Quick notes:
- Customer is asking for an evidence-based carveout for 'customer-managed network transit, peering misconfigurations, and vendor transit provider incidents.'
- My read: reasonable if we keep the evidence bar tight and require mutually agreed traces + provider incident confirmation. We should avoid language that creates a broad 'network issues don't count' escape hatch.

Suggested approach for draft:
1) Define narrow list of excluded components (VPC peering config, customer edge routers, named third-party transit providers).
2) Require 3 pieces of corroborating evidence (Redwood server-side logs/KV cache timings + customer-provided packet captures or traceroutes + either the transit provider incident ticket or BGP feeds).
3) Retain Redwood's right to perform parallel diagnostics and to postpone credit determinations pending evidence review (48–72h).

Any additions/concerns? Also thinking we should include a short "dispute resolution" clause for attribution disagreements (escalation to engineering sync with a 5-business-day calendar).

-J
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Patel <samira@oriontech.com>, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 09:14:00 -0700 (PDT)
Subject: Proposed wording: "Network Attribution Addendum" (draft attached)

Hi Samira — attached is a draft addendum that captures the narrow carveout and the evidence requirements Jasmine mentioned. Key points in short:
1) Excluded components: customer-managed peering, customer edge routers, and named third-party transit providers listed in Appendix A.
2) Evidence required: a minimum of two independent data sources: (a) Redwood service telemetry demonstrating the service-level degradation window; (b) customer-provided network traces or provider incident ticket showing degradation/packet loss; optional (c) transit provider BGP/ticket as corroboration.
3) Attribution timeline: both parties share initial diagnostics within 72 hours; final credit determination within 10 business days unless parties agree otherwise.

Attachment: SLA_Addendum_draft.docx

Please review and tell us where you'd like tighter/looser language. If acceptable, we can convert to DocuSign-ready addendum and circulate to procurement.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: Amit Rao <amit@oriontech.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, Samira Patel <samira@oriontech.com>
Cc: legal@oriontech.com
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 11:02:00 +0530
Subject: RE: Proposed wording: "Network Attribution Addendum" (draft attached)

Vivek / Jasmine — thanks for the quick turnaround. Legal reviewed and proposed one minor redline: replace references to 'customer-managed network transit' with 'customer-managed network transit and third-party transit providers engaged by customer' to make sure incidents on contracted transit carriers are covered by the attribution process. We've attached a redline.

We're OK with the evidence list but would like a slightly longer attribution timeline for cross-border coordination — propose 15 business days (to accommodate provider support windows).

Attachment: orion-redlines.docx

If you accept the redline and timeline extension we'll ask procurement to sign once we have a DocuSign link.

Best,
Amit Rao
Deputy GC, OrionTech
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Rao <amit@oriontech.com>, Samira Patel <samira@oriontech.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 26 Aug 2027 19:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Proposed wording: "Network Attribution Addendum" (draft attached)

Amit/Samira — thanks for the feedback and the redline. Vivek/Irene and I reviewed internally:
- We can accept the redline wording that explicitly calls out customer-contracted transit providers.
- To be cooperative on international support windows we agree to a 12-business-day attribution resolution window (compromise from your 15 / our 10).

Next steps: we'll update the doc, generate a DocuSign envelope, and send to your procurement/legal. Expect the DocuSign link in the next 24 hours.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/tx/abc123-orion-sla-addendum
Confluence draft: https://redwood.company/confluence/OT-priv-vpc-sla

Thanks — looking forward to closing this so we can proceed with the Private deployment.

-Jasmine
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
